alex_support: Heads-up — customer 'rsa-medical' is hitting sporadic TLS handshake failures to our private inference endpoints (hosted in us-west-2). They see 502s and gRPC stream resets after applying a new firewall hardening policy. Any quick checks?
meera_k: Which VPC/subnet? Are they using our Private deployment or Dedicated?
alex_support: Private (customer-managed VPC peering). Subnet: 10.20.0.0/22. NAT via a single NAT instance. They said failures started after they tightened outbound rules.
james_sre: Can you paste a client-side curl/openssl error from their repro? That helps narrow TLS vs TCP.
ingrid_repro: Customer sent this snippet: ```curl 'https://inference.rsa-medical.private.redwood-inference.com/predict' -v
* About to connect() to inference.rsa-medical.private.redwood-inference.com port 443
*   Trying 198.51.100.45...
* Connected to inference.rsa-medical.private.redwood-inference.com (198.51.100.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* error:14094410:SSL routines:SSL3_READ_BYTES:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL read: errno=104```
meera_k: "tlsv1 alert unknown ca" suggests either client can't validate cert or SNI mismatch pulling back a different cert (or a TLS intercepting proxy). Do they have TLS inspection?
ajames_sre: Also check NACLs. If outbound ephemeral ports are blocked then connections can start but fail during handshake/renegotiation. Ask them to paste SG and NACL outbound rules.
ingrid_repro: They sent ACL snippets — pasted: ```# Security Group outbound
0.0.0.0/0 TCP 443 ALLOW
# NACL outbound (stateless)
Rule 100: 0.0.0.0/0 DENY TCP 32768-65535
Rule 110: 0.0.0.0/0 ALLOW TCP 80,443```
meera_k: Bingo. NACL denies the ephemeral port range (32768-65535). Because NACLs are stateless, return traffic needs the ephemeral range allowed both directions. Right now the server can accept the SYN but return packets get dropped by the NACL. That can show up as SSL errors/short reads.
ajames_sre: Quick repro command we usually ask them to run from a private instance in the same subnet: ```# from customer host
curl -v --resolve inference.rsa-medical.private.redwood-inference.com:443:198.51.100.45 https://inference.rsa-medical.private.redwood-inference.com/healthz
# and
ss -tn sport :443 state established | grep 198.51.100.45
# tcpdump on nat instance: tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 198.51.100.45 and port 443 -w /tmp/trace.pcap```
ingrid_repro: Customer ran the tcpdump — they see SYN, SYN-ACK from model host, then final ACK from customer host is missing (gets dropped). NAT instance logs show RSTs when ephemeral port is not reachable.
alex_support: Actionable items for them: 1) Update NACL to ALLOW ephemeral range outbound+inbound (32768-61000 or 1024-65535 depending on platform), 2) Ensure NAT gateway (or instance) has no iptables rule blocking high ports, 3) Check TLS inspection boxes — if there is an SSL proxy replace cert chain or bypass for our host. 4) Confirm control-plane egress allowlist includes the model host IPs or domain (in case they maintain an allowlist).
meera_k: I'll paste a suggested minimal NACL policy to share: ```# Allow ephemeral return traffic
Inbound: Rule 100 ALLOW 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 32768-65535
Outbound: Rule 100 ALLOW 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 32768-65535
# Keep HTTP/HTTPS
Inbound: Rule 110 ALLOW 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 443
Outbound: Rule 110 ALLOW 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 443
# Deny everything else at end
```
ajames_sre: Also remind them to verify TLS with SNI explicitly: ```openssl s_client -connect 198.51.100.45:443 -servername inference.rsa-medical.private.redwood-inference.com -showcerts
# expect leaf cert with CN/SAN matching inference.rsa-medical.private.redwood-inference.com```
ingrid_repro: Customer updated NACL to allow ephemeral 32768-61000 both ways and replaced NAT instance iptables that were dropping high ports. They report streams are stable now. :tada:
deploy-bot: Incident closed: private-inference-rsa-medical - root cause: customer NACL denied ephemeral outbound ports causing TLS handshake failures. Tags: networking, support, remediation
